# Project Setup and General Notes


## SQL Server Databases

Historically, SQL Server has been used as the primary method for storing and securing the data used to create the model (at least since 2015).   Interim steps in building the model relied on a mixture of SQL queries along with manual edits and data manipulation in Excel.

Microsoft Access front ends facilitated easy interaction with the database tables, in particular SQL queries.  However, interim and lookup tables were stored in database table objects with queries and imports linking across project folders.   Access front ends were housed on share separate from project files.  Drive letters in links mean team members needed be aligned (or link will break).

**Permissions and Access**

Dan Ebenal to grant access to \\alder\S52018$.   Individuals granted access also needed to be part of the BC Stats VPN group (request to Liam) 

Microsoft SQL Server (SSMS) downloaded from here: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/ssms/download-sql-server-management-studio-ssms?view=sql-server-ver16#download-ssms](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/ssms/download-sql-server-management-studio-ssms?view=sql-server-ver16#download-ssms).  Software Center seems to have an older version, this one was suggested in a document compiled by Jon for another project.   

Each year we ask IT to create a new database on decimal.idir.bcgov for the new year’s PSSM.  The database name could be anything, but historically has followed the pattern PSSMYYYY, where YYYY is the first prediction year. 

**Historical Database Cleanup**

A general principle is to keep one older version of the STP data work for reference purposes while producing a newer version of the model.  The naming convention is PSMXXXX, reflecting the first year in the project folder associated with the model.

PSSM2015 has some lookup tables that were used for a lifetime earnings calculation program run for PSFS.  It relied on Census data and may be a handy reference.   Suggestion to move out to csv files or moved to newer db.   Current access restricts creating table objects

PSSM2017 previous model version kept for reference in case some analytical backwards steps would be more effective than methods used in PSSM 2019.  See PSSM 2019-2020 Future Enhancements.docx for further insights here.  Current access restricts creating table objects

PSSM2021 was created for this year’s model (will need to change name at some point).  Owners can read data from existing tables and create new tables prefixed with our IDIR.

_Sometimes the linked SQL tables in the Access databases run too slowly or not at all (depending on what’s going on with the network) so converted the tables to local Access tables as a workaround.  In order to get the data back into the SQL tables import the local Access table into SQL server and then run a SQL query to update the SQL version of the table. Make sure that you set up an ODBC connection for the PSSM SQL Server database so that you can link to it from Access._

## MSAccess Databases

MS Access databases live on alder share at S52018$ ([\\alder](file://alder)).  Each database corresponds to a sub analysis, or key component of work, often associated with one or two datasets. Each component of work has a corresponding workflow document in the main project folder, under _development->documentation_

Access databases contain linked tables to the Student Outcomes data in ORACLE.  Select people can access these and access was granted to myself through Student Outcomes Team.  To access the tables. Connect into Citrix Workspace.  They do not appear to be accessible outside of that workspace.  Student Outcomes tables are owned by INFORWARE, and are preceded with “INFOWARE_”. A best practice is to create a static copy for querying, so as not to accidentally write to tables sitting in ORACLE.

Each year, the ORACLE tables under go changes and so we need to work with Sheila to get the correct ORACLE tables and possibly refresh links.  A list of changes since 2019, including code books with the most recent codes for applicable variables are here: Also included are the BGS BC CIP Cluster variables.

## R Code Scripts

2023 changes include migrating the workflow to R from SQL Server projects + Access Databases + Excel in an attempt to streamline the process.

R code will be stored in the BC Gov repository, postsecondary-supply-model: [https://github.com/bcgov/post-secondary-supply-model](https://github.com/bcgov/post-secondary-supply-model)

Raw data will continue to be housed in the SQL Server database “PSSM2023” on decimal.  Scripts to access and clean the data will be housed in the github repository.  Two packages: “configure” and “safepaths” contain helper functions which allow users to securely access the data, which is protected under ISA.

## ORACLE and SQL Developer

Student Outcomes data requires connecting to ORACLE database, DEV01.World.  If required, follow these steps:

1.       Install the oracle client.  This can be done by running the windows installer found here: J:\PGMS\Oracle\Older Oracle Files\11g\Oracle_Client11g_11.2.0.1.0_Gen_P0.  It should also be available from the software center.

2.       Copy and paste the following connection info into your tnsnames.ora file, depending on your client it may be located here: C:\ORACLE\ORAHOME_11g\network\admin

3.       If you are connecting via R and using the package RJDBC (see section R, below) then the Java JDK Development Kit may also be required.  This is to enable one dependency package, RJava.  At one point it was available in the Software center, but in November 2024, OCIO gave out instructions to upgrade to a newer version directly from the Oracle site: [www.oracle.com/ca-en/java/technologies/downloads/#jdk23-windows](http://www.oracle.com/ca-en/java/technologies/downloads/#jdk23-windows).

## Beyond20/20

In order to read .ivt file format from Statistics Canada, this requires Beyond 20/20 Professional Browser. Steps for downloading: [Beyond 20/20 Professional Browser (statcan.gc.ca)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/public/beyond20-20). Can also review online user guides (several others can be found on the web): [https://datalib.usask.ca/dli/beyond_2020/v7.0_sp4/Beyond2020_Browser_UserGuideShort.pdf](https://datalib.usask.ca/dli/beyond_2020/v7.0_sp4/Beyond2020_Browser_UserGuideShort.pdf "https://datalib.usask.ca/dli/beyond_2020/v7.0_sp4/Beyond2020_Browser_UserGuideShort.pdf")

# ==============================================================================
# PSSM Combined Reference Script
# ==============================================================================
# BC Government Post-Secondary Supply Model (PSSM)
#
# This file combines ALL R scripts from the R/ directory into a single
# reference document for new analysts to understand the full pipeline.
#
# IMPORTANT: This file is NOT meant to be run as-is. The real pipeline uses
# source() to run individual scripts in sequence. See README.md for details.
#
# Pipeline Sequence:
#   01a-01d  Preprocessing (enrolment + credential data cleaning)
#   02a      Program matching (CIP codes, APPSO/BGS/DACSO datasets)
#   02b-07   Model runs x3 (cohorts -> near-completers -> grad projections ->
#            PTIB -> program projections -> occupation projections)
#   08       Report generation (Excel workbooks)
#
# Entry point: run_all_three_model_runs.r (near the end of this file)
#   It orchestrates three sequential model runs:
#     1. Regular/Fresh Run (prep-for-fresh-run.R)
#     2. QI Run (prep-for-qi-run.R)
#     3. PTIB Run (prep-for-ptib-run.R)
#
# Each numbered script (02b-07) has a paired load-*.R data loader that
# pre-fetches required data from the database before analysis.
#
# Do NOT run numbered scripts (02b-07) independently - they are designed to
# be sourced by the orchestrator prep scripts and depend on flags:
#   regular_run, qi_run, ptib_run (TRUE/FALSE)
# ==============================================================================




# ── DOMAIN REFERENCE NOTES ──────────────────────────────────────
# Use the onboarding guide as the source of truth for current infrastructure
# and model concepts: R + SQL Server on decimal + LAN files are active; Access,
# Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# Core model roles: STP supplies enrolment/credential records; Student Outcomes
# supplies labour and occupation distributions; Census fills graduate-level gaps;
# PTIB adds private training institution estimates.
# Preserve CIP, NOC, region, school-year, PSI, and student identifier fields as
# character wherever possible to avoid losing leading zeros or special codes.
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ==============================================================================



---

## R/SQL chunk

```r
# FILE: utils.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      utils.R
# Stage:       Utility / orchestration support
# Runs after:  Called by prep scripts and run_all_three_model_runs.r
# Key inputs:  script path passed to time_execution(); file_logger
# Key outputs: console/logger timing and error tracebacks
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Defines the pipeline timing/error wrapper used by the orchestrator.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.



# Define the time_execution function to track execution time and handle errors
# source(file_path, echo = TRUE, keep.source = TRUE):
#   
#   echo = TRUE: Prints each line of code as it is executed, helping to trace progress and identify errors.
# keep.source = TRUE: Retains source references to each line, which can improve the accuracy of the traceback.
# local = TRUE: Executes in a local environment, preventing side effects on the global environment (optional but useful for modularization).
# traceback(): After an error, traceback() provides a stack trace that shows the line numbers and function calls leading up to the error, making it easier to identify the specific line in the sourced file that caused the issue.
# Log File Connection: log_conn <- file(log_file, open = "a") opens a connection in append mode to add logs to execution_log.txt.
# 
# Logging Each Step:
#   
#   Start: Logs a start message with a timestamp before running the script.
# Completion: Logs the completion message with the elapsed time after successful execution.
# Error: Logs the error message and writes the traceback() to the log file for debugging.
# finally Block: Ensures the log file connection is closed after execution, even if an error occurs.
# 
# Custom Log File: You can specify a custom log file by passing a different path to log_file.

# By default, source() runs the code in a new environment, so variables defined in the global environment (like log_file) are not accessible within that sourced script unless explicitly passed or the globalenv is specified.
# To make all global variables accessible within each source() call, set local = globalenv(). This allows the sourced file to inherit the global environment variables, including log_file and file_logger:
# ── Function: time_execution() ──────────────────────────────────
# Purpose: Source one pipeline script with consistent start/end logging and
#          error capture so long model runs can be audited later.
# Parameters:
#   file_path (character): Path to the R script to source.
# Returns: Whatever source() returns; the practical output is logging.
# Side effects: Sources into globalenv(), prints progress, and writes errors and
#               tracebacks through futile.logger's file_logger.
# ⚠️ NOTE: globalenv() is intentional because run flags and shared objects must
#          be visible across sourced scripts.


time_execution <- function(file_path) {
  # Log a start message with a timestamp
  flog.info(paste("Starting:", file_path), name = "file_logger")
  
  # Log a start message with a timestamp
  print(
    "#################################################################################################"
  )
  print(paste(Sys.time(), "Starting:", file_path))
  print(
    "#################################################################################################"
  )
  
  start_time <- Sys.time()
  
  tryCatch({
    # Source the file with echo, and log each line to the log file
    source(
      file_path,
      echo = TRUE,
      keep.source = TRUE,
      # local = TRUE
      local = globalenv()) # Make global variables accessible in source
    
    # Log the completion message with elapsed time
    end_time <- Sys.time()
    elapsed <- end_time - start_time
    print("########################################################################")
    print(paste(
      Sys.time(),
      "Completed:",
      file_path,
      "in",
      round(elapsed, 2),
      "seconds"
    ))
    print("########################################################################")
    flog.info(paste("Completed:", file_path, "in", round(elapsed, 2), "seconds"),
              name = "file_logger")
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Log the error message if execution fails
    error_message <- paste(Sys.time(), "Error in file:", file_path, " - ", e$message)
    print("###############################################")
    print(error_message)
    print("###############################################")
    # Log the error message if execution fails
    flog.error(paste("Error in file:", file_path, "-", e$message), name = "file_logger")
    flog.error(traceback(), name = "file_logger")  # Log the traceback for details
    
    stop()
  }
 )
}



# ==============================================================================



---
```

## STP Data

**2023 Data, notes, and learnings**

STP data request was submitted mid-May to ECC, requested same fields as last time (see below).

_Enrolment File:_ A data load script in R was used to define column types and load into PSSM2023 MS SQL Server database on DECIMAL.  Merging of tables back to a single enrollment table can be done on the SQL Server.  Load script to be housed on GitHub.

Requested a csv with metadata (ECC data warehouse table definition) and a small data sample of 100 rows to configure our load scripts.  Data requested included the following fields.

PSI_PEN, PSI_BIRTHDATE, PSI_GENDER, PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_FRST_CNTACT, TRUE_PEN, ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN, PTY_ID, STP_ALT_ID, LAST_SEEN_BIRTHDATE, LAST_SEEN_GENDER, BC_K_12_STUDENT_EVER, LAST_SEEN_ABOR_EVER_FLAG, LAST_SEEN_SCHOOL_YEAR, LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_NUMBER, LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME, LAST_SEEN_STUDENT_GRADE, LAST_SEEN_SP_NEED_CODE, GRAD_YEAR_MONTH, GRAD_DISTRICT_NUMBER, GRAD_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME, GRAD_COLLEGE_REGION, GRADUATION_CREDENTIAL_NAME, AGPA_PCT, ATTENDING_PSI_OUTSIDE_BC, LAST_SEEN_HOME_LANG, LAST_SEEN_NON_RES_FLAG, PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR, PSI_REG_TERM, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_CURR, PSI_ABORIGINAL_STATUS, PSI_NEW_STUDENT_FLAG, PSI_ENROLMENT_SEQUENCE, PSI_CODE, PSI_TYPE, PSI_FULL_NAME, PSI_BASIS_OF_ADMISSION, PSI_MIN_START_DATE, PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, PSI_PROGRAM_CODE, PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_CIP_CODE, EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_FACULTY, PSI_CE_CRS_ONLY, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY, PSI_VISA_STATUS, PSI_STUDY_LEVEL, PSI_ENTRY_STATUS, OVERALL_ABORIGINAL_STATUS

The following data field names had been updated since 2019:

PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_FRST_CNTACT, PTY_ID, LAST_SEEN_SP_NEED_CODE, GRAD_DISTRICT_NUMBER, GRAD_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME, GRAD_COLLEGE_REGION, GRADUATION_CREDENTIAL_NAME, AGPA_PCT, LAST_SEEN_HOME_LANG, PSI_REG_TERM, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_CURR, PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_CE_CRS_ONLY

Fieldnames PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, PSI_CE_CRS_ONLY, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_CURR and PSI_REG_TERM were replaced with non-truncated versions.

Additionally, we received:

·         LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_NAME in place of LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME,

·         new column: AT_GRAD_DISTRICT_NUMBER

PTY_ID was not supplied this time.

Outstanding Q’s for data provider:

·         Are EFFECTIVE_DATE (2019 data) and PSI_EFFECTIVE_DATE (2023 data) the same data?

·         Are AT_GRAD_CREDENTIAL_NAME (2019 data) and CREDENTIAL_NAME (2023 data) the same data?

·         What does AT_GRAD_CURRENT_REGION refer to?

·         What does PTY_ID (2019 data) refer to?

Non-UTF8 data found in PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC were removed manually prior to uploading to SQL via R. Due to the size of the datasets, time to upload from R was long, around 28,000 rows per minute, depending on network speed etc. 

The connection to decimal appears to terminate when Windows instructs the PC to go to sleep.  The time to sleep can be updated in Windows power and sleep settings.  

_Credential File_: A data load script can also be written in R but splitting likely not required.  Requesting csv with metadata (ECC data warehouse table definition).  Data to include the following fields:

PTY_ID, CREDENTIAL_AWARD_DATE, PSI_CODE, PSI_FULL_NAME, PSI_PEN, PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER, PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR, PSI_PROGRAM_CODE, PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY, PSI_CREDENTIAL_LEVEL, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CIP, PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN, STP_ALT_ID

Changes in 2023: 

·         We received a new column, SNAPHOT_DATE. 

·         PTY_ID wasn’t included

**2019/2017 data specifications and use**

Historically projections have relied on data from 2002/2003 to the most recent complete set of data available.  For 2019-2020 model, the project relied on data from 2002/03 to 2018/2019.  For 2013/2014 model (year == first year of predicted supply) data was requested for 2002/03 to 2013/14.  (The last year of data was discarded as was an incomplete year). 

_Credential File_

•     Credential Data (STP_Award) was obtained from PSFS for the 2019/2020 PSSM as a tabular data file. As a first step in the pre-processing, this file was uploaded into PSSM2019 to STP_Credential table.

•     STP_Credential contains 1057538 rows (0.29) and includes the following fields:

PTY_ID, CREDENTIAL_AWARD_DATE, PSI_CODE, PSI_FULL_NAME, PSI_PEN, PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER, PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR, PSI_PROGRAM_CODE, PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY, PSI_CREDENTIAL_LEVEL, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CIP, PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN, STP_ALT_ID

•     ~ (1.5%) that have null Encrypted True Pen have a non-null PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER and PSI_CODE instead to identify an individual.

_Enrolment File_

•     Enrolment Data was obtained from PSFS for the 2019/2020 PSSM as a tabular data file.  As a first step in the pre-processing, this file was uploaded into PSSM2019 to STP_Enrolment table.  The field “ID” was added to uniquely identify each record.  All the fields from the STP txt file were included in case extra analysis was requested. An additional field “psi_birthdate_cleaned” added, presumably during the data load process.

•     STP_Enrolment contains 14,236,521 (8.12GB db storage) and includes the following fields:

PSI_PEN, PSI_BIRTHDATE, PSI_GENDER, PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_FRST_CNTACT, TRUE_PEN, ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN, PTY_ID, STP_ALT_ID, LAST_SEEN_BIRTHDATE, LAST_SEEN_GENDER, BC_K_12_STUDENT_EVER, LAST_SEEN_ABOR_EVER_FLAG, LAST_SEEN_SCHOOL_YEAR, LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_NUMBER, LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME, LAST_SEEN_STUDENT_GRADE, LAST_SEEN_SP_NEED_CODE, GRAD_YEAR_MONTH, GRAD_DISTRICT_NUMBER, GRAD_DISTRICT_LONG_NAME, GRAD_COLLEGE_REGION, GRADUATION_CREDENTIAL_NAME, AGPA_PCT, ATTENDING_PSI_OUTSIDE_BC, LAST_SEEN_HOME_LANG, LAST_SEEN_NON_RES_FLAG, PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR, PSI_REG_TERM, PSI_STUD_POSTAL_CD_CURR, PSI_ABORIGINAL_STATUS, PSI_NEW_STUDENT_FLAG, PSI_ENROLMENT_SEQUENCE, PSI_CODE, PSI_TYPE, PSI_FULL_NAME, PSI_BASIS_OF_ADMISSION, PSI_MIN_START_DATE, PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC, PSI_PROGRAM_CODE, PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_CIP_CODE, EFFECTIVE_DATE, PSI_FACULTY, PSI_CE_CRS_ONLY, PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY, PSI_VISA_STATUS, PSI_STUDY_LEVEL, PSI_ENTRY_STATUS, OVERALL_ABORIGINAL_STATUS

# FILE: load-stp-enrol.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-stp-enrol.R
# Stage:       Source data loading
# Runs after:  before 01a
# Key inputs:  LAN STP enrolment files; decimal config
# Key outputs: STP_Enrolment
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Loads raw STP enrolment records to SQL Server using character-safe schemas.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.

# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at

# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

# ******************************************************************************
# Load STP enrolment data from staging area in LAN project folder, to decimal.  
# Requested data to be in tab-separated text files partitioned by school year.
# The hope if that smaller datasets are more easily processed by R and SMSS
# ******************************************************************************
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(config)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")

fls <- list.files(glue::glue("{lan}/data/stp/STP_ISA_PSSM"), full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)
fls <- fls[grepl("STP_ENROLMENT", fls)]

# ---- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                 Driver = db_config$driver,
                 Server = db_config$server,
                 Database = db_config$database,
                 Trusted_Connection = "True")

# ---- Define Schema ----
schema <- 
  schema(PSI_PEN = string(),
       PSI_BIRTHDATE = string(),
       PSI_GENDER = string(),
       PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER = string(),
       PSI_STUDENT_POSTAL_CODE_FIRST_CONTACT = string(),
       TRUE_PEN = string(),
       ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN = string(),
       STP_ALT_ID = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_BIRTHDATE = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_GENDER = string(),
       BC_K_12_STUDENT_EVER = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_INDIGENOUS_EVER_BACKDATED = string(), # data codes also different
       LAST_SEEN_SCHOOL_YEAR = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_NUMBER = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_DISTRICT_NAME = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_STUDENT_GRADE = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_SPECIAL_NEED_CODE = string(),
       GRAD_YEAR_MONTH = string(),
       AT_GRAD_DISTRICT_NUMBER = string(),
       AT_GRAD_DISTRICT_NAME = string(),
       AT_GRAD_CURRENT_COLLEGE_REGION_NAME = string(),
       AT_GRAD_CURRENT_COLLEGE_REGION_NUMBER = string(),
       CREDENTIAL_NAME = string(),
       AGPA_PERCENT = string(),
       ATTENDING_PSI_OUTSIDE_BC = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_HOME_LANGUAGE = string(),
       LAST_SEEN_RESIDENCY = string(),
       PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR = string(),
       PSI_REGISTRATION_TERM = string(),
       PSI_STUDENT_POSTAL_CODE_CURRENT = string(),
       PSI_INDIGENOUS_STATUS = string(),
       PSI_NEW_STUDENT_FLAG = string(),
       PSI_ENROLMENT_SEQUENCE = string(),
       PSI_CODE = string(),
       PSI_TYPE = string(),
       PSI_FULL_NAME = string(),
       PSI_BASIS_OF_ADMISSION = string(),
       PSI_MIN_START_DATE = string(),
       PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION = string(),
       PSI_PROGRAM_CODE = string(),
       PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE = string(),
       PSI_CIP_CODE = string(),
       PSI_FACULTY = string(),
       PSI_CONTINUING_EDUCATION_COURSE_ONLY = string(),
       PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY = string(),
       PSI_VISA_STATUS = string(),
       PSI_STUDY_LEVEL = string(),
       PSI_ENTRY_STATUS = string(),
       OVERALL_INDIGENOUS_STATUS = string()
      )

# ---- Write to decimal ----
invisible(lapply(fls[1], 
                 write_to_decimal, 
                 con = con,  
                 schema = schema, 
                 append = TRUE))

# ---- Functions ----
# ── Function: write_to_decimal() ────────────────────────────────
# Purpose: Read one STP source file with an explicit Arrow schema and write it
#          to the target SQL Server table.
# Parameters:
#   flnm (character): Full path to the STP source file.
#   con (DBI connection): Open SQL Server connection.
#   schema (arrow schema): Expected column names and types.
#   append (logical): Whether to append to the existing table.
#   format (character): Source file format, usually 'tsv'.
# Returns: NULL/invisible; progress is printed.
# Side effects: Writes rows to STP_Enrolment in SQL Server.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Code and ID fields are kept as character to preserve leading zeros.
write_to_decimal <- function(flnm, con, schema, append = FALSE, format = "tsv"){
  
  tblnm <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(flnm))
  cat(glue::glue("Processing {tblnm}: {Sys.time()} ..."))
  cat()
  
  data <- open_dataset(sources = flnm,
                     format = format, 
                     schema = schema, 
                     skip = 1)
  
  DBI::dbWriteTableArrow(con, 
                    name = "STP_Enrolment", 
                    nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(data), 
                    append = append)
  
  cat(glue::glue("...completed {Sys.time()}"))
  cat("\n")
  
}

# ---- Disconnect ----
dbDisconnect(con)




# ==============================================================================



---
```

# ******************************************************************************
# Load STP credential data from staging area in LAN project folder, to decimal.  
# Requested data to be in tab-separated text file
# STP credential data loads with a few data type conversion problems: 
#   - querying SQL data returns PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESC as a quoted string
#   - dates are uploaded format YY-MM-DD instead of YYYY-MM-DD
# ******************************************************************************
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(config)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")
raw_data <- glue::glue("{lan}/data/stp/STP_ISA_PSSM/STP_CREDENTIAL_2023.dsv")

## ----- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                 Driver = db_config$driver,
                 Server = db_config$server,
                 Database = db_config$database,
                 Trusted_Connection = "True")

# ---- Define Schema ----
schema <- 
  schema(CREDENTIAL_AWARD_DATE = string(),
         PSI_CODE = string(),
         PSI_FULL_NAME = string(),
         PSI_PEN = string(),
         PSI_STUDENT_NUMBER = string(),
         PSI_SCHOOL_YEAR = string(),
         PSI_PROGRAM_CODE = string(),
         PSI_PROGRAM_EFFECTIVE_DATE = string(),
         PSI_CREDENTIAL_CATEGORY =string(),
         PSI_CREDENTIAL_LEVEL = string(),
         PSI_CREDENTIAL_CIP = string(),
         PSI_CREDENTIAL_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION = string(),
         SNAPSHOT_DATE = string(),
         ENCRYPTED_TRUE_PEN = string(),
         STP_ALT_ID = string())

# ---- Write to decimal ----
tblnm <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(raw_data))
cat(glue::glue("Processing {tblnm}: {Sys.time()} ..."))

data <- open_dataset(
  sources = raw_data, 
  format = "tsv",
  schema = schema,
  skip = 1
)

dbWriteTableArrow(con, 
                  name = "STP_Credential", 
                  nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(data), append = TRUE)

cat(glue::glue("...completed {Sys.time()}"))
cat("\n")


# ---- Disconnect ----
dbDisconnect(con)







# ==============================================================================



---

## Documentation context


## INFOWARE TABLES

**2023 Data Notes and Learnings:**

INFOWARE tables are used throughout the data model and is directly accessible by select BC Stats employees.  However, due to the sensitive nature of some of the data, access is restricted and so we should have an idea of why we need each table before requesting access.  Connect with Student Outcomes Teams for access. 

Noting also that some of these tables are out of date.  Another rationale for understanding data requirements before requesting access.

The design of the project is such that the password is added to a configuration file, which is shared via a file on a secure LAN drive.  As access to the outcomes data is granted on an individual basis, the LAN was not a good place for this, as access to the LAN is generally contingent on signing the STP ISA.   The approach has worked for us as a team in terms of automation/coding and collaboration but doesn’t align with existing SO team protocols. 

It was decided that, given the sensitivity of the data, the frequency of so data updates, and the design of the R project, we would send SQL to SO team (Sheila Richards-Brown) and she would provision that data via J:\TRANSFER.  A single R script will then upload this data directly to SQL Server.

**2019 Data Notes:**

Linked tables are found in the Microsoft Access databases used in the 2019 model: W:\PSSM\21-825-8 Post-Secondary Supply Model 2019-2020.  A short list was pulled using only the Access queries used in building the model.  This doc contains column names, INFOWARE table names and the database name which they are used in.  Database name roughly equates to the data analysis step or submodel.

[P:\PSSM\25-1319 Post-Secondary Supply Model 2022-2023\development\sql\ db-infoware-tables.xlsx](file:///P:/PSSM/25-1319%20Post-Secondary%20Supply%20Model%202022-2023/development/sql/db-infoware-tables.xlsx)

**NOC codes**

In the last model run, several queries were used which involved NOC codes.  INFOWARE tables containing NOC code variables were used in two analysis steps: a) the CIP-toNOC work and b) pulling the cohort data.  Below is the INFOWARE table name and column containing NOCS used in analysis.  Other sources with NOC codes include the Stats Can Census data

_CIP-NOC_Top10_2015to19:_ PSSM cohorts data (for DACSO, APPSO and BGS) are used to create a CIP-NOC database for AEST and a set of Excel files with tables and graphs for NOC to CIP and CIP to NOC.

1.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_CD

2.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_DESCRIPTION

3.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_LNC2_CD

4.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_LNC2_DESCRIPTION

5.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_LNC3_CD

6.       INFOWARE_L_NOC_4DIGITS       LNOC_LNC3_DESCRIPTION

_PSSM_2019-2020_Cohorts:_  Student Outcomes cohort and survey data are pulled here from the Oracle Infoware Schema.  Done for APPSO, DACSO and BGS. During the process the step derives the labour supply and other required variables for the PSSM.

1.       INFOWARE_APPRENTICE_SHORT_RESP                  NOC_CD

2.       INFOWARE_BGS_DIST                                                    NOC

3.       INFOWARE_C_OUTC_CLEAN_SHORT_RESP           LABR_OCCUPATION_LNOC_CD

4.       INFOWARE_TRADES_SHORT_RESP                           NOC_CD

CIP to NOC top 10 work

## Student Outcomes Data

Student Outcomes Data is split over four (4) survey datasets.  Master data is kept in Oracle data warehouse (INFOWARE tables)

Datasets are cleaned and released in 5-year chunks as fully labeled SPSS file at case level by Student Outcomes team.  Excel versions are also available with documentation, pivot tables and dataset. The latest release contains data for 2019 to 2023 survey years. Either SPSS or Excel can be obtained from Outcomes Survey Team (Sheila Richards-Brown).

Option to pull data directly from the ORACLE tables was recommended by Ian.  The outcomes data is used in many steps throughout the model process and so we need a more customized approach.  Additionally, there is a requirement for 6 years of data.

It was decided that, given the sensitivity of the data, the frequency of SO data updates, and the design of the R project, we would send SQL to SO team (Sheila Richards-Brown) and she will provision that data via J:\TRANSFER.  A single R script will then upload this data directly to SQL Server.

CIP/NOC 2016 vs 2021 Standards:  The latest release of student outcomes data includes NOC 2016 and 2021.  NOC (4) is mapped to the survey data based on students’ self-reported information.  The mapping is done using master tables from Stats Canada.  We will use NOC 2021 standards.

As of May 2024, CIP is coded using 2016 standards as Ministry of Advanced Education has not switched yet.  As CIP (2016) is available from Stats Canada, we are okay still to use the earlier CIP codes.

2016 NOC (4) contains ~500 codes.  In the latest release of the BGS file they only used 438 codes, however this can change with updates.  XXXX is a NOC code that hasn’t been identified for the student. Some teachers have 403X because we don’t know the level.  

**BGS**

BGS uses an expanded version of BC Program Clusters;  Arts and Sciences is broken out into four (4) more clusters.  For program matching, we need the following tables from Student Outcomes (SO).

·         INFOWARE_BGS_COHORT_INFO

·         INFOWARE_BGS_DIST_xx_yy

·         INFOWARE_BGS_PROGRAMS

For the cohort data itself, we need the following tables:

·         INFOWARE_BGS_COHORT_INFO: here we filter on column ‘subm_cd’ for required years. Also, srv_y_n  = 0 or 1.

·         INFOWARE_BGS_DIST (renamed from INFOWARE_BGS_DIST_15_29)

·         t_bgs_inst_recode

**DACSO**

For program matching, we need the following tables from Student Outcomes (SO).  Sheila from SO reported no structural changes to these tables since last model run.

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_2DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_PROGRAMS : data for years 1994 – 2023. Master programs table contains all programs seen in DAC, APP and TFTRV.

·         INFOWARE_PROGRAMS_HIST_PRGMID_XREF: data for years 2009 – 2023. Program ID cross reference table for updated CPCs, DAC, APP and TFTRV

For the cohort data itself, we need the following tables:

·         INFOWARE_C_OUTC_CLEAN2:

·         INFOWARE_PROGRAMS

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016: filter out records where lcip_lcippc_name is Developmental or Personal Improvement and Leisure.

·         INFOWARE_C_OUTC_CLEAN2_SHORT_RESP

·         INFOWARE_SURV_COHORT_COLLECTION_INFO: filter on column ‘coci_subm_cd’ for required years (C_Outc06-23)

**APPSO**

For the cohort data pull, we need the following tables:

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_APPRENTICE_SHORT_RESP

·         INFOWARE_APPRENTICE_COHORT_INFO: here we filter on column ‘subm_cd’ for required years

·         INFOWARE_PROGRAMS

**TRD**

For the cohort data pull, we need the following tables:

·         INFOWARE_PROGRAMS

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016

·         INFOWARE_TRADES_COHORT_INFO: here we filter on column ‘subm_cd’ for required years

·         INFOWARE_TRADES_SHORT_RESP

# FILE: load-outcomes-data.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-outcomes-data.R
# Stage:       Source data loading
# Runs after:  before cohort loading and 02a/02b
# Key inputs:  provisioned Student Outcomes CSVs
# Key outputs: Student Outcomes *_raw tables
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Loads APPSO, BGS, DACSO, TRD, and lookup extracts into SQL Server.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.

# Copyright 2024 Province of British Columbia
# 
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the &quot;License&quot;);
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
# 
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software distributed under the License is distributed on an &quot;AS IS&quot; BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

##########################################################################################################################################
# This script loads student outcomes data for students who students who 
# TRD: were formerly enrolled in a trades program (i.e. an apprenticeship, trades foundation program or trades-related vocational program)
# APP: have completed the final year of their apprenticeship technical training within the first year of graduation.
# BGS: recently graduated with a Baccalaureate degree (Baccalaureate students are surveyed two years after graduation)
# DAC: recently graduated after completing programs at public colleges, institutes, and teaching-intensive universities (~18 months prior)

# The following data sets are read into SQL server from a csv housed in the project LAN drive. 
# Original data is sourced from the student outcomes survey database, and provisioned to the project by the student outcomes survey team.
#   Q000_TRD_DATA_01: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (a few duplicates)
#   Q000_TRD_Graduates: a count of graduates by credential type, age and survey year
#   T_APPSO_DATA_Final: unique survey responses for each person/survey year  (a few duplicates)
#   APPSO_Graduates: a count of graduates by credential type, age and survey year
#   BGS_Data_Update: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (for years since last model run)
#   t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (for years since last model run)
#   infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp
#   tmp_tbl_Age_AppendNewYears
#   INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016
#   INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016
#############################################################################################################################################

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# notes: 
#   (small n) minor differences in code description/name: INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016, INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016
#   (small n) differences in prgm_credential: T_DACSO_DATA_Part_1_stepA
#   I've read that using assign() as below is fragile ... it works though, so..?
#   TODO: investigate both tmp_table_Age and the BGS data a little more.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(config)
library(RODBC)
library(DBI)

# set up db connection and lan paths
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
decimal_con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                 Driver = db_config$driver,
                 Server = db_config$server,
                 Database = db_config$database,
                 Trusted_Connection = "True")
# make sure vpn is on, and the lan is available. Or switch to safepath approach. 
use_schema <- config::get("myschema")
lan = config::get("lan")
so_lan_path <- glue::glue("{lan}/data/student-outcomes/csv/so-provision/")

# read csv's into objects in memory.
so_data_all_full_pathnames <- list.files(so_lan_path, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
tmp_table_age_full_pathnames <- list.files(so_lan_path, pattern = "qry_make_tmp_table_Age_step1_20[0-9][0-9].csv", full.names = TRUE)

# read all files into current environment, processing tmp_table_Age_step1_20xx data sets separately.
so_data_full_pathnames <- so_data_all_full_pathnames[!so_data_all_full_pathnames %in% tmp_table_age_full_pathnames] 
so_data_full_pathnames %>%  
  set_names(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(so_data_full_pathnames))) %>% 
  map(read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  imap(~ assign(..2, ..1, envir = .GlobalEnv)) %>%
  invisible()

# tmp_table_Age_step1_20xx datasets
qry_make_tmp_table_Age_step1 <- tmp_table_age_full_pathnames %>%  
  set_names(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(tmp_table_age_full_pathnames))) %>% 
  map(read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types="dcdcd") %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  invisible()

# sanity check: any datasets missing from current environment?
so_data_expected <- c(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(so_data_full_pathnames)),'qry_make_tmp_table_Age_step1')
missing <- !so_data_expected %in% ls()

if(any(missing)) {
  warning("One or more SO datasets were not loaded into current environment.")
}

# recast datatypes
APPSO_Data_01_Final$PEN <- as.character(APPSO_Data_01_Final$PEN)
APPSO_Data_01_Final$APP_TIME_TO_FIND_EMPLOY_MJOB <- as.numeric(APPSO_Data_01_Final$APP_TIME_TO_FIND_EMPLOY_MJOB)

BGS_Q001_BGS_Data_2019_2023$PEN = as.character(BGS_Q001_BGS_Data_2019_2023$PEN)

DACSO_Q003_DACSO_DATA_Part_1_stepA <- DACSO_Q003_DACSO_DATA_Part_1_stepA %>% 
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Cast identifier/code fields to character before joins or uploads so leading zeros and special codes are preserved.
  mutate(across(.cols = c(TPID_LGND_CD, COCI_PEN),  
                .fns = as.character))

Q000_TRD_DATA_01 <- Q000_TRD_DATA_01 %>% 
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Cast survey identifiers and grouped status codes to character before combining Student Outcomes sources.
  mutate(across(.cols = c(GRADSTAT_GROUP, PEN),  
                .fns = as.character)) 

INFOWARE_C_OutC_Clean_Short_Resp <- INFOWARE_C_OutC_Clean_Short_Resp %>% 
  mutate(across(.cols = c(TTRAIN, Q08, FINAL_DISPOSITION, RESPONDENT, CREDENTIAL_DERIVED),  
                .fns = as.character)) 

# remove non-standard characters so ssms won't throw an err
INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016$LCP4_DESCRIPTION <- iconv(INFOWARE_L_CIP_4DIGITS_CIP2016$LCP4_DESCRIPTION, "UTF-8", "UTF-8", sub ='')
INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016$LCIP_NAME <- iconv(INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016$LCIP_NAME, "UTF-8", "UTF-8", sub ='')
INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016$LCIP_DESCRIPTION <- iconv(INFOWARE_L_CIP_6DIGITS_CIP2016$LCIP_DESCRIPTION, "UTF-8", "UTF-8", sub ='')

# load to ssms
so_data_expected[!missing] %>% 
  mget(envir = .GlobalEnv)  %>% 
  imap(~ dbWriteTable(decimal_con, overwrite = TRUE, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{use_schema}"."{..2}_raw"')), value = ..1))

# ==============================================================================

---
```

# This script loads student outcomes data for students who students who have completed the 
# final year of their apprenticeship technical training within the first year of graduation.
# 
# The following data is read from SQL server database:
#   T_APPSO_DATA_Final: unique survey responses for each person/survey year  (a few duplicates)
#   APPSO_Graduates: a count of graduates by credential type, age and survey year
library(tidyverse)
library(RODBC)
library(config)
library(glue)
library(DBI)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")
my_schema <- config::get("myschema")

# ---- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
decimal_con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                 Driver = db_config$driver,
                 Server = db_config$server,
                 Database = db_config$database,
                 Trusted_Connection = "True")

# ---- Read outcomes data ----
# source(glue::glue("./sql/02b-pssm-cohorts/appso-data.sql"))
T_APPSO_DATA_Final <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."APPSO_DATA_01_Final_raw"')))
APPSO_Graduates_dat <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."APPSO_Graduates_raw"')))

# Convert some variables that should be numeric
T_APPSO_DATA_Final <- T_APPSO_DATA_Final %>% 
  mutate(TTRAIN = as.numeric(TTRAIN))

# Make sure this is updated to only the last 6 years of data 
T_APPSO_DATA_Final <-
  T_APPSO_DATA_Final %>% 
  mutate(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE =  case_when (
    CURRENT_REGION1 %in% 1:8 ~ CURRENT_REGION1, 
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 5 ~ 9,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 6 ~ 10,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 7 ~ 11,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 8 ~ -1,
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Standardize detailed respondent ages into PSSM age-group labels so cohorts can be combined across survey sources.
  mutate(AGE_GROUP_LABEL = case_when (
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 15:16 ~ "15 to 16",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 17:19 ~ "17 to 19",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 20:24 ~ "20 to 24",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 25:29 ~ "25 to 29",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 30:34 ~ "30 to 34",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 35:44 ~ "35 to 44",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 45:54 ~ "45 to 54",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 55:64 ~ "55 to 64",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 65:89 ~ "65 to 89",
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Store the numeric age-group index used by downstream SQL lookups and projection joins.
  mutate(AGE_GROUP = case_when (
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 17:19 ~ 2,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 20:24 ~ 3,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 25:29 ~ 4,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 30:34 ~ 5,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 35:44 ~ 6,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 45:54 ~ 7,
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 55:64 ~ 8,
    TRUE ~ NA)) %>%
  # 📌 CONTEXT: NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY is the model-ready labour supply flag used in weighted cohort distributions.
  # ⚠️ NOTE: This intentionally follows source-specific survey response logic; confirm definitions before changing categories.
  mutate(NEW_LABOUR_SUPPLY = case_when(
    APP_LABR_EMPLOYED == 1 ~ 1,
    APP_LABR_IN_LABOUR_MARKET == 1 & APP_LABR_EMPLOYED == 0 ~ 1,
    APP_LABR_EMPLOYED == 0 ~ 0,
    RESPONDENT == '1' ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ 0))

# When running, make sure to update weights for the regular run. 
# Replace the weights in the appropriate area in the code (~lines 71-77):
  

if (regular_run == TRUE | ptib_run == T){
  T_APPSO_DATA_Final <-
    T_APPSO_DATA_Final %>% 
    mutate(WEIGHT = case_when (
      SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc19' ~ 1,
      SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc20' ~ 2,
      SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc21' ~ 3,
      SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc22' ~ 4,
      SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc23' ~ 5,
      TRUE ~ 0)) 
} 

if (qi_run == TRUE ) {
  # check that these years are correct
  # TODO: this moved out of query for derived weights  but means an extra step for QI - move back to query design?
  T_APPSO_DATA_Final <-
    T_APPSO_DATA_Final %>% mutate(WEIGHT = case_when (
    SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc19' ~ 2,
    SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc20' ~ 3,
    SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc21' ~ 4,
    SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc22' ~ 5,
    SUBM_CD == 'C_Outc23' ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ 0)) 
}

# prepare graduate dataset
APPSO_Graduates_dat  %>%
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Store the numeric age-group index used by downstream SQL lookups and projection joins.
  mutate(AGE_GROUP = case_when (
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 15:16 ~ "15 to 16",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 17:19 ~ "17 to 19",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 20:24 ~ "20 to 24",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 25:29 ~ "25 to 29",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 30:34 ~ "30 to 34",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 35:44 ~ "35 to 44",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 45:54 ~ "45 to 54",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 55:64 ~ "55 to 64",
    APP_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 65:89 ~ "65 to 89",
    TRUE ~ NA)) -> APPSO_Graduates_dat 

dbWriteTable(decimal_con, 
             name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."T_APPSO_DATA_Final"')), 
             value = T_APPSO_DATA_Final,
             overwrite = TRUE)

dbWriteTable(decimal_con, 
             name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."APPSO_Graduates"')),
             value = APPSO_Graduates_dat, 
             overwrite = TRUE)

dbDisconnect(decimal_con)

# ==============================================================================

---

# FILE: load-cohort-bgs.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-cohort-bgs.R
# Stage:       Cohort data loading
# Runs after:  before 02a BGS and 02b
# Key inputs:  BGS raw data and lookups
# Key outputs: T_BGS_Data_Final; T_Weights
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Prepares BGS survey records for matching and cohort distributions.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.

# Copyright 2024 Province of British Columbia
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

# This script loads student outcomes data for students who students who recently graduated with a 
# Baccalaureate degree (Baccalaureate students are surveyed two years after graduation)
#
# The following data set is read from SQL server database:
#   BGS_Data_Update: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (for years since last model run)
#
# The following data sets are read into SQL server from the LAN:
#   T_BGS_Data: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (last model run) 
#   T_weights: carried forward from last models run and updated with new data.  Waiting for confirmation
#   T_BGS_INST_Re-code: look-up used to re-code several institution codes
#
# Notes: T_BGS_Data +  BGS_Data_Update contain the full set of survey responses used. 
# T_BGS_Data_Final_2017.csv used for 2019 model run, T_BGS_Data_Final.csv for 2023 model run (rollover)
# Some changes to variable names were done for consistency and will be needed when using 2023 BGS_Data_Final
# use query BGS_Q001_BGS_Data_2019_2023 for 2023 model run but note overlapping years (2019)

library(tidyverse)
library(RODBC)
library(config)
library(DBI)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")
# source("./sql/02b-pssm-cohorts/bgs-data.sql")

# ---- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
decimal_con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                         Driver = db_config$driver,
                         Server = db_config$server,
                         Database = db_config$database,
                         Trusted_Connection = "True")
# should specify the DBO schema for final run, individual IDIRS for testing
schema <- config::get("myschema")

# ---- Read LAN Data ----
# Lookups
T_weights  <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/t_weights.csv"), 
                  col_types = cols(Group = "d", Weight = "d", WeightQI = "d", .default = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")

tmp_BGS_INST_REGION_CDS <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/tmp_BGS_INST_REGION_CDS.csv"), 
                  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")

T_BGS_INST_Recode <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_BGS_INST_Recode.csv"), 
                  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")

# ---- Read Outcomes Data ----
if (regular_run == T | ptib_run == T) {
  BGS_Data_Update <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."BGS_Q001_BGS_Data_2019_2023_raw"')))

  BGS_Data_Update <- BGS_Data_Update %>% 
    # 📌 CONTEXT: Rename BGS fields to the common PSSM cohort vocabulary used by later Student Outcomes scripts.
    rename("FULL_TM_WRK" = FULL_TM, 
           "FULL_TM_SCHOOL" = D03_STUDYING_FT, 
           "IN_LBR_FRC" = LBR_FRC_LABOUR_MARKET,
           "EMPLOYED" = LBR_FRC_CURRENTLY_EMPLOYED,
           "UNEMPLOYED" = LBR_FRC_UNEMPLOYED,
           "TRAINING_RELATED" = E10_IN_TRAINING_RELATED_JOB, 
           "TOOK_FURTH_ED" = D01_R1) %>% # this can be added to original query
    mutate(AGE_17_34 = if_else(between(AGE, 17, 34), 1, 0)) %>%
    mutate(OLD_LABOUR_SUPPLY = NA) %>% # I don't think we use this?
    select(-c(D02_R1_CURRENTLY_STUDYING, SUBM_CD)) # nor these?
  
  BGS_Data_Update <- BGS_Data_Update %>%
    mutate(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE =  case_when (
      REGION_CD %in% 1:8 ~ REGION_CD, 
      CURRENT_REGION %in%c(6,9,10) ~ 10,
      CURRENT_REGION == 7 ~ 11,
      CURRENT_REGION == 5 ~ 9,
      CURRENT_REGION == 8 ~ -1,
      TRUE ~ NA)) 
  
  BGS_Data_Update <- BGS_Data_Update %>% 
    # 📌 CONTEXT: Attach institution-region fallback values for cases where respondent current-region fields are missing or outside BC.
    inner_join(tmp_BGS_INST_REGION_CDS, by = join_by(INST)) %>%
    mutate(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE = 
             if_else((CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE == -1 | is.na(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE)) &
                       (SRV_Y_N == 0 | is.na(SRV_Y_N)), as.numeric(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM), CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE))
  
  # ---- Make T_BGS_Data_Final ----
  T_BGS_Data_Final <- BGS_Data_Update %>% 
    select(-c(CUR_RES,REGION_CD,CURRENT_REGION))
}

# ---- Write to decimal----
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{schema}"."T_Weights"')), value = T_weights, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{schema}"."T_BGS_INST_Recode"')), value = T_BGS_INST_Recode, overwrite = TRUE)

if (regular_run == T | ptib_run == T) {
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{schema}"."T_BGS_Data_Final"')), value = T_BGS_Data_Final, overwrite = TRUE)

}

# ---- Clean Up ----
dbDisconnect(decimal_con)

# ==============================================================================

---
```

# FILE: load-cohort-dacso.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-cohort-dacso.R
# Stage:       Cohort data loading
# Runs after:  before 02a DACSO and 02b
# Key inputs:  DACSO raw data and lookups
# Key outputs: DACSO working and lookup tables
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Loads DACSO survey/lookup data and SQL Server column typing.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.

# Copyright 2024 Province of British Columbia
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

# This script loads student outcomes data for students who students who recently graduated after
# completing programs at public colleges, institutes, and teaching-intensive universities (~18 months prior)
#
# The following data-set is read from SQL server database:
#   t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (for years since last model run)
#   infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp: 
#
# The following data-sets are read into SQL server from the LAN:
#   tbl_Age: bins ages into groups (1-10)
#   tbl_Age_Groups: used to assign a label to each age group.
#   t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes_bc: loo-up re-codes maps regions
#   t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes: look-up re-codes maps regions
#   t_current_region_pssm_codes: look-up re-codes maps regions
#   tbl_noc_skill_level_aged_17_34: used SQL server for upload as this file contains non-supported type characters
#   T_PSSM_Credential_Grouping: a static table for relabeling credential names
#   T_year_survey_year: TO DO
#   T_Cohorts_Recoded:  this contains survey records for all years.  The table is refreshed in the workflow.
# 
# Notes: tbl_noc_skill_level_aged_17_34: used SQL server for upload as this file contains 'non-supported' type characters.
#   T_year_survey_year is carried forward from last models run and updated with new data. 
#   T_Cohorts_Recoded: can instead just be created each year.  See comments in 02b-pssm-cohots-dacso.R
#   Age group labels are assigned in the script.  There are two different groupings used to group students by age in the model, 
#    check the groupings are the same in DACSO, APPSO etc cohorts

library(tidyverse)
library(RODBC)
library(config)
library(DBI)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")

# ---- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
decimal_con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                         Driver = db_config$driver,
                         Server = db_config$server,
                         Database = db_config$database,
                         Trusted_Connection = "True")
# should specify the DBO schema for final run, individual IDIRS for testing
my_schema <- config::get("myschema")

# ---- retrieve data from decimal ----
infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp_dat <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp_raw"')))

# ---- Read raw data from LAN ----
tbl_Age_Groups <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/tbl_Age_Groups.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
tbl_Age_Groups_Rollup <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/tbl_Age_Groups_Rollup.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
tbl_Age <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/tbl_Age.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
T_PSSM_Credential_Grouping <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_PSSM_Credential_Grouping.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
t_year_survey_year <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/t_year_survey_year.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
t_cohorts_recoded <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/rollover/02/T_Cohorts_Recoded.csv"), 
                  col_types = cols(PEN = "c", STQU_ID = "c", Survey = "c", LCIP_CD = "c", LCP4_CD = "c", NOC_CD = "c", INST_CD = "c",
                                   PSSM_Credential = "c",  PSSM_CRED = "c", LCIP4_CRED= "c",  LCIP2_CRED = "c", .default = col_number()), n_max = 1) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
t_current_region_pssm_codes <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_Current_Region_PSSM_Codes.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_Current_Region_PSSM_Rollup_Codes.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes_bc <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_Current_Region_PSSM_Rollup_Codes_BC.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps")
T_NOC_Broad_Categories <- 
  readr::read_csv(glue::glue("{lan}/development/csv/gh-source/lookups/02/T_NOC_Broad_Categories_Updated.csv"), col_types = cols(.default = col_guess())) %>%
  janitor::clean_names(case = "all_caps") 

# ---- Write LAN data to decimal ----
# Note: may want to check if table exists instead of using overwrite = TRUE
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."tbl_Age_Groups"')), value = tbl_Age_Groups, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."tbl_Age_Groups_Rollup"')), value = tbl_Age_Groups_Rollup, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."tbl_Age"')), value = tbl_Age, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."T_PSSM_Credential_Grouping"')), value = T_PSSM_Credential_Grouping, overwrite = TRUE)

dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."T_NOC_Broad_Categories"')), value = T_NOC_Broad_Categories, overwrite = TRUE) 
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_year_survey_year"')), value = t_year_survey_year, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_cohorts_recoded"')), value = t_cohorts_recoded, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_current_region_pssm_codes"')), value = t_current_region_pssm_codes, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes"')), value = t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes_bc"')), value = t_current_region_pssm_rollup_codes_bc, overwrite = TRUE)

# --- Read SO DACSO data and write to decimal ----

if (regular_run == T | ptib_run == T) {
t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."DACSO_Q003_DACSO_DATA_Part_1_stepA_raw"')))
dbWriteTableArrow(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp"')), infoware_c_outc_clean_short_resp_dat, overwrite = TRUE)

dbWriteTableArrow(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa"')), value = t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa, overwrite = TRUE)

dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ADD CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE FLOAT NULL")
dbExecute(decimal_con,"UPDATE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa
                       SET CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE =  
                          CASE
                            WHEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION1 IN (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8) THEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION1
                            WHEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION4 = 5 THEN 9
                            WHEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION4 = 6 THEN 10
                            WHEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION4 = 7 THEN 11
                            WHEN TPID_CURRENT_REGION4 = 8 THEN -1
                            ELSE NULL
                            END;")

dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ALTER COLUMN TTRAIN INT NULL")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ALTER COLUMN LABR_EMPLOYED INT NULL")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ALTER COLUMN COSC_GRAD_STATUS_LGDS_CD INT NULL") # check these
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ALTER COLUMN COSC_GRAD_STATUS_LGDS_CD_GROUP INT NULL") # check these
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa ALTER COLUMN RESPONDENT INT NULL")
rm(t_dacso_data_part_1_stepa)
gc()
}

dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE T_NOC_Broad_Categories ALTER COLUMN BROAD_CATEGORY_CODE NVARCHAR(50) NULL;")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE T_NOC_Broad_Categories ALTER COLUMN MAJOR_GROUP_CODE NVARCHAR(50) NULL;")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE T_NOC_Broad_Categories ALTER COLUMN SUB_MAJOR_GROUP_CODE NVARCHAR(50) NULL;")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE T_NOC_Broad_Categories ALTER COLUMN MINOR_GROUP_CODE NVARCHAR(50) NULL;")
dbExecute(decimal_con, "ALTER TABLE T_NOC_Broad_Categories ALTER COLUMN UNIT_GROUP_CODE NVARCHAR(50) NULL;")

# ---- Clean Up ---
dbDisconnect(decimal_con)
# rm(list = ls())

                

# ==============================================================================

---

# FILE: load-cohort-trd.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-cohort-trd.R
# Stage:       Cohort data loading
# Runs after:  before 02b
# Key inputs:  TRD raw tables
# Key outputs: T_TRD_DATA; TRD_Graduates
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Standardizes Trades outcomes records and graduate age groups.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.

# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through

# This script loads student outcomes data for students who students who were formerly enrolled in 
# a trades program (i.e. an apprenticeship, trades foundation program or trades-related vocational program)
#
# The following data sets are read into SQL server from the student outcomes survey database:
#   Q000_TRD_DATA_01: unique survey responses for each person/survey year (a few duplicates)
#   Q000_TRD_Graduates: a count of graduates by credential type, age and survey year
#
# Notes: Age group labels are assigned.  Note there are two different groupings used to group students by age in the model.

library(tidyverse)
library(RODBC)
library(config)
library(glue)
library(DBI)

# ---- Configure LAN and file paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")

# ---- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
decimal_con <- dbConnect(odbc::odbc(),
                         Driver = db_config$driver,
                         Server = db_config$server,
                         Database = db_config$database,
                         Trusted_Connection = "True")
# should specify the DBO schema for final run, individual IDIRS for testing
schema <- config::get("myschema")

# ---- Read raw data and disconnect ----
#source(glue::glue("./sql/02b-pssm-cohorts/trd-data.sql"))

Q000_TRD_DATA_01 <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."Q000_TRD_DATA_01_raw"')))
Q000_TRD_Graduates <- dbReadTable(decimal_con, SQL(glue::glue('"{my_schema}"."Q000_TRD_Graduates_raw"')))

# Convert some variables that should be numeric
Q000_TRD_DATA_01 <- Q000_TRD_DATA_01 %>% 
  mutate(GRADSTAT = as.numeric(GRADSTAT), 
         KEY = as.numeric(KEY),  
         TTRAIN = as.numeric(TTRAIN))

# Gradstat group : couldn't find in outcomes data so defining here.
Q000_TRD_DATA_01 <- Q000_TRD_DATA_01 %>% 
  mutate(LCIP4_CRED = paste0(GRADSTAT_GROUP, ' - ' , LCIP_LCP4_CD , ' - ' , TTRAIN , ' - ' , PSSM_CREDENTIAL))

Q000_TRD_DATA_01 <-
  Q000_TRD_DATA_01 %>% 
  mutate(CURRENT_REGION_PSSM_CODE =  case_when (
    CURRENT_REGION1 %in% 1:8 ~ CURRENT_REGION1, 
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 5 ~ 9,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 6 ~ 10,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 7 ~ 11,
    CURRENT_REGION4 == 8 ~ -1,
    TRUE ~ NA)) 

# prepare graduate dataset
Q000_TRD_Graduates   %>%
  # 📌 CONTEXT: Standardize detailed respondent ages into PSSM age-group labels so cohorts can be combined across survey sources.
  mutate(AGE_GROUP_LABEL = case_when (
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 15:16 ~ "15 to 16",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 17:19 ~ "17 to 19",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 20:24 ~ "20 to 24",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 25:29 ~ "25 to 29",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 30:34 ~ "30 to 34",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 35:44 ~ "35 to 44",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 45:54 ~ "45 to 54",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 55:64 ~ "55 to 64",
    TRD_AGE_AT_SURVEY %in% 65:89 ~ "65 to 89",
    TRUE ~ NA)) -> Q000_TRD_Graduates 

dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{schema}"."T_TRD_DATA"')), value = Q000_TRD_DATA_01, overwrite = TRUE)
dbWriteTable(decimal_con, name = SQL(glue::glue('"{schema}"."TRD_Graduates"')), value = Q000_TRD_Graduates, overwrite = TRUE)

dbDisconnect(decimal_con)

# ==============================================================================

---
```

# Combined section: load-custom-stats-can.R


## Documentation context


## Stats Canada Data Request

**2023 Notes, decisions, and learnings**

PSSM model relies on custom census data. 

_CIP_

CIP and NOC standards have undergone major structural revisions.   We are requesting the Major Field of Study variable be based on CIP Canada 2016 to remain in alignment with PSFS, BC Outcomes and STP. 

Major field of study write-in responses were assigned codes using the revised CIP Canada 2021 (variable CIP2021) as well as the older CIP Canada 2016 (variable CIP2011) to facilitate historical comparisons. Since the CIP 2016 is directly comparable to CIP 2011, the CIP2011_2 variable allows comparisons between the 2021 Census, 2016 Census, and 2011 National Household Survey. They will use the CIP Canada 2016 historical for the tabulation of this request.

Some series and their subcomponents are not used in the CIP variables: series 21, 32 to 37 and 53.

_NOC_

NOC codes will change from the traditional 4-digit format to a new 5-digit format. The new NOC 2021 contains 516 occupations, up from the 500 unit groups included in the NOC 2016. Of those 516 unit groups, 400 have a one-to-one correspondence with a unit group from the NOC 2016. 

[https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Versions/ChangesNoc?objectid=NsNwJRqWS9JiVGOp1%2FrC8A%3D%3D](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca/Versions/ChangesNoc?objectid=NsNwJRqWS9JiVGOp1%2FrC8A%3D%3D)

Both NOC 2016 and 2021 are available in the student outcomes data, so we can forecast skilled labour supply using either classification system.  For 2023 model we are requesting data from the 2021 census. 

Statistics Canada has confirmed that having the 5-digit codes in a census table won’t affect 4-digit code suppression. They mentioned there may still be suppression at the 4-digit level, but it would happen regardless of there being 5-digit codes in the same census table or not. I will clarify that you only wish to have the 2021 NOC and confirm the quote and timeline.  

_Order Details:_

Table Title:          Non-Immigrant Population Aged 17 to 64 Years in Private Households with Location of Study as B.C. by Age (4), Highest Certificate, Diploma or Degree (7), Labour Force Status (4), Attendance at School (3), Major Field of Study (BC Program Cluster aggregation of CIP 2016) (10) and Occupation - Unit group - National Occupational Classification (NOC) 2021 (821) for Canada, British Columbia, its Economic Regions (10) and Selected area aggregates, 2021 Census, 25% Sample-based Data

Requested format: Beyond 20/20

A csv version of the data from Beyond20/20 (e.g., ivt format provided by Stat Can) was exported. The data was opened in Beyond20/20, the occupation/NOC seemed to be the default first column, and the rest were the university degrees, masters, etc. counts. The geography, age groups, and major field of study were manually dragged to the left of the occupation column. Then file > save as csv – update the file name, file type, and desired location – click OK.

![A screenshot of a computer
Description automatically generated]

The attendance and labour force were not moved/included in the above table.  

Note: issue with header (funky apostrophe in master’s in one header) when exported to csv from Beyond20/20 and uploaded into R. Used locale=locale(encoding="latin1") in read_csv; the geography column had weird en-dashes that translated to \u0096, also updated those in the cleanup. This is completed in the load-custom-stats-can.R script.

Two other cuts of the data were saved from the data from Beyond20/20 (e.g., ivt format provided by Stat Can) was exported. The data was opened in Beyond20/20, the occupation/NOC seemed to be the default first column, and the rest were the credentials: university degrees, masters, etc. counts. The age groups, geography and major field of study were manually dragged to the left of the occupation column. The occupation column was moved out of the table. The labour force and school attendance was moved below the university etc. header. Then the credential variable was moved between age and geography. Then file > save as xls. This is the first unfiltered cut of the data. For the next, you will leave the columns/rows etc. as they are, but right click on Occupation/NOCs. Then you will click on ‘Search’ for All occupations.

 ![A screenshot of a computer
Description automatically generated]

Note: These will be saved on the LAN for the time being and used to manually manipulate them for use in the Labour_Distributions table used later in the process.

**2019 Data Specifications**

Requested data variables are: Age (4), Highest Certificate, Diploma or Degree (7), Labour Force Status (4), Attendance at School (3), Major Field of Study (BC Program Cluster aggregation of CIP 2016) (10) and Occupation –National Occupational Classification (NOC) 2016 (693A) for Canada, British Columbia, its Economic Regions (10) and Selected area aggregates, 2016 Census, 25% Sample-based Data

CIP codes have been rolled up into a higher grouping referred to as the “BC Program Cluster”. 

·         Major Field of Study comes from CIP BC Program Clusters – an amalgamation of 2-digit CIPS.  CIP Clusters (10) come from PSFS (formerly Ministry of Advanced Education). 

·         NOC 2016 (693A) refers to 4-digit NOC plus three roll-up totals

```r
# FILE: load-custom-stats-can.R
# ==============================================================================
# ── PIPELINE POSITION ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Script:      load-custom-stats-can.R
# Stage:       Census data loading
# Runs after:  before run-imputation-by-region.R
# Key inputs:  custom Statistics Canada CSV
# Key outputs: STAT_CAN
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Loads custom Census data used for graduate-level distributions.
# 📌 CONTEXT: Current PSSM processing uses R, SQL Server on decimal, and LAN files.
#             Access, Citrix, and \alder\S52018$ are historical references only.
# ⚠️ NOTE: This combined file is a reference document; run source scripts through
#          the orchestrator or documented sequence, not as one monolithic script.

# Copyright 2024 Province of British Columbia
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

# ******************************************************************************
# Load custom Statistics Canada data from staging area in LAN project folder, to decimal.  
# ******************************************************************************

# ---- libraries and global variables
library(arrow)
library(tidyverse)
library(odbc)
library(DBI)
library(janitor)

# ---- Configure LAN Paths ----
lan <- config::get("lan")
raw_data_file <- glue::glue("{lan}/data/statcan/stat-can-data-export.csv")

# ----- Connection to decimal ----
db_config <- config::get("decimal")
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                 Driver = db_config$driver,
                 Server = db_config$server,
                 Database = db_config$database,
                 Trusted_Connection = "True")

# ---- Read raw data  ----
raw_data <- read_csv(raw_data_file, locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))

# ---- Clean data ----
data <- raw_data %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  rename(age_group = age,
         occupation_NOC = occupation,
         masters_degree_and_earned_doctorate = master_s_degree_and_earned_doctorate # funky apostrophe header name
  ) %>% 
  # fix the geography column en-dashes
  mutate(geography = str_replace(geography,"\u0096","-"))

# ---- Write to decimal ----
dbWriteTableArrow(con,
                  name = "STAT_CAN",
                  nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array_stream(data))

# ---- Read from decimal ----
dbReadTable(con, "STAT_CAN")

# ---- Disconnect ----
dbDisconnect(con)

# ==============================================================================

---
```
